chunks: It is an unwanted visitor, an invincible adversary and an unaccounting killer. Its ropes have entrapped you, its evils have surrounded you, its arrowheads have aimed at you, its sway over you is great, its oppression on you is continuous and the chance of its missing you is remote.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the nature and inevitability of death in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Account of those who remain apprehensive of death,' Imam Ali (AS) personifies Death as an uninvited, undefeated, and relentless adversary that has ensnared humanity with its bonds and overwhelming authority. This description highlights the inevitability of death as a universal decree, reinforcing the Shia theological view of death not as an end, but as a transition (barzakh) where the soul is seized by the Angel of Death. The imagery of 'bonds' and 'assault' underscores the inescapable nature of this divine command, urging believers to prepare spiritually for this inevitable encounter.
